instruction: You are given `/home/user/Desktop/subdyn_base.fst`, `/home/user/Desktop/subdyn_oc3_base.dat`, and an NREL 5 MW OC3 dependency set. Complete a fixed-base SubDyn reaction-load analysis from the command line. 1. Write `/home/user/Desktop/build_case.py`. Create `/home/user/Desktop/subdyn.dat` from the supplied SubDyn template, retain its fully fixed mudline reaction joint, and request the native SubDyn channels `ReactFXss` and `ReactMYss`. 2. Create `/home/user/Desktop/elasto_subdyn.dat`, `/home/user/Desktop/aero_subdyn.dat`, and `/home/user/Desktop/servo_subdyn.dat` from the supplied module files and normalize their dependency paths to the desktop `5MW_Baseline` tree. Create `/home/user/Desktop/subdyn_case.fst` from the main template; set `TMax=30`, `CompSeaSt=0`, `CompHydro=0`, `CompSub=1`, `DT_Out=0.1`, `OutFileFmt=1`, and point `EDFile`, `AeroFile`, `ServoFile`, and `SubFile` to the generated files. 3. Run `/home/user/miniconda3/bin/openfast subdyn_case.fst`, retain `/home/user/Desktop/subdyn_case.out`, and save the console output as `/home/user/Desktop/subdyn_case.log`; require normal termination. 4. Write `/home/user/Desktop/postprocess.py` and use samples with `t >= 20 s` to compute mean `ReactMYss`; the glue-code channel is in N*m, so divide by `1e6` for MN-m. Compute mean `ReactFXss`; its channel is in N, so divide by `1000` for kN. Save `/home/user/Desktop/summary.txt` as one row `mean_reactmyss_mnm,mean_reactfxss_kn`. Do not use GUI tools.
